Which output format should you pick?

OBJ

The safest hand-off to Blender, ZBrush, CAD, or a render engine. Vertices are merged, faces are indexed, and almost everything imports it.

PLY

A compact ASCII mesh with an explicit vertex/face header. Useful for scan processing, research code, and tools that dislike OBJ.

Binary STL

The normal slicer format: 50 bytes per triangle, small and fast. Re-export it when a converter produced an unnecessarily huge ASCII file.

ASCII STL

Readable and diffable, but several times larger. Useful for debugging a mesh or checking coordinates by eye, not for production.

Client work stays client-side

Cloud converters ask you to upload a model before they will hand back a file. For a commissioned miniature, an unreleased product, or a scan of a person, that is a data-sharing decision disguised as a utility. This converter has no upload step at all: the bytes are read from your disk, converted in memory, and written back as a download.

Nothing is stored between visits. There is no account, no history, no server-side copy, and no watermark added to the output. When you close the tab, the mesh is gone.

STL conversion questions

Formats, welding, units, and what conversion does not fix.

Does this STL converter upload my file?

No. The STL is read locally with FileReader, converted in memory, and saved with a Blob download. There is no upload request and no server-side converter. Your model can be confidential and still never leave the machine.

Which formats can I convert to?

STL input works in both binary and ASCII. You can export OBJ, ASCII PLY, binary STL, or ASCII STL. Binary STL is the smallest and is what most slicers prefer; OBJ and PLY are useful for sculpting, rendering, and scan tools.

Can it convert OBJ or PLY back into STL?

Not in this build. This page accepts STL input and exports OBJ, PLY, binary STL, or ASCII STL. If you need the reverse direction, send a note through the feedback form and it will be considered for the next update.

What is the vertex merge tolerance?

STL stores every triangle with its own three vertices, so shared corners are duplicated. Before writing OBJ or PLY, the converter merges vertices that fall within the tolerance - 0.001 mm by default. Raise it for messy scans, lower it for very fine details.

Does conversion change the model's size or units?

No. Coordinates are copied one-to-one. STL files do not contain units, and this converter does not guess or rescale them. If a model is 25.4 times too small, it was probably authored in inches; fix the scale in the slicer or with the Scale Inspector.

Does converting repair a broken mesh?

No. Conversion is a format change, not a repair. Open edges, non-manifold geometry, and inconsistent winding survive the round trip. Run the file through the STL Printability Checker before you slice it.
